A dining experience I have never had. In all my years. In any country. Potential customers be forewarned
Feb 2020 • Solo
I was feeling something tempura so stopped in to try this place. Unfortunately, the experience began poorly with 2 Japanese men smoking like chimneys in this very small place that didn’t ease up even after their food arrived. To make matters worse, after ordering some shrimp tempura and stir fried “vegetables,” the dish arrived like a mushy mess and included helpings of pork, which were noted nowhere in the description (I can’t eat pork). When I asked the server about it she simply shrugged her shoulders and refused to remove it and walked away. I continued to eat the one dish I ordered, while the other one not ordered remained on the corner of the table. As such, I anticipated perhaps another “discussion” as to that was not the dish described but was unprepared to what followed. The server left and returned with the bill with both dishes being charged. I explained why I felt it unfair but the served, raising her voice noe, insisted I pay for
it all. I told her it was not clear and I can’t eat pork, so said I would pay for all the rest before laying down cash to cover what I ate as well as ½ of the pork dish. As I proceeded to leave the server ran in front of me in an attempt to block my exit. Again, I was left shocked and said she should move as I want to leave, though she did not. I brushed past her and got in my motorbike. She ran out chasing after now picking up a big stick from which she swung at me breaking the mirror off my motorbike. The Japanese owner then came out (he had been sitting in the restaurant the whole time) apologizing and said I should leave as the server continued to yell profanities. 

Having lived in Saigon for nearly 20 years I am well aware of local customs and etiquette —and occasional irrational women— but I have never in all my time here, nor back in the west for that matter, ever had such an experience with total disregard to customer service, not least attacking them. Needless to say, both my local and foreign friends will hear about this establishment as well as others in Saigon’s dynamic dining scene. That said, there are numerous dining and drinking establishments, including Japanese ones, that offer exceptional dining experiences. Unfortunately, Chokotto at 42 Phạm Viết Chánh, Quận Bình Thạnh is not one of them.

炒飯、野菜炒め、餃子は美味しい。
ラーメンは味が薄くイマイチでした。

手軽に中華を食べたい時にはおススメです！

英語表記は「Chokotto」、日本語表記は「ちょっと」。
どっちが正しいのかは分かりません。。。

A Japanese-style Chinese restaurant located in pham viet chanh.
 Fried rice, fried vegetables, dumplings are delicious.
 The ramen taste was so thin that it was not good enough.

 It is recommended when you want to eat Chinese food easily!
